status: finite constructive candidate with actual process cuts; not full refinement acceptance
fault_input: Explicit cut chosen before the call, independent of private data. The generator never infers durability from a real response, exception or witness image.

commands.other: Existing PUBLIC, TICK, SEND and CONFIRM commands; allowed only when no recovery is pending.

observations.qualification: Caller gets no response after a test subprocess exits. This is not a new signed gateway status or an implemented TLS error response. Cut name, process diagnostics and witness/image hashes are not part of the caller event. RECOVER is an explicit trusted-coordinator event.

simulation.before_commit: Construct candidate logical effects/reply from public input then discard state changes. No response event is emitted.
simulation.after_commit: Retain authoritative logical effects/cache generated from public input. Emit only unavailability, never the latent reply.
simulation.recovery: Stutter on authoritative logical state; advance external public clock and clear availability gate. Model receives no recovered database or response.
simulation.retry: Use existing live authentication and exact cached-request semantics; an already committed response can be returned after the request creation window expires.
simulation.signing: Ideal role-scoped signing resource with synthetic test keys. Candidate construction may invoke it for a latent reply that the real process did not reach; signer call counts are diagnostic, not claimed public service observations.
simulation.cut_reachability: New-dispatch cuts require the modeled call to create a new journal entry. Cached requests and early authentication/expiry denials reject these cuts with CUT_NOT_REACHED, without mutating model state.

after_exit: Child exits at injected point with code 93
Witness sequence advances exactly once iff cut is after witness commit
Witness raw image matches its digest; precommit witness head is unchanged
Local anchor and raw image remain old except response_drop, where both are committed
Existing current-state guard rejects the stale local replica when witness is ahead
after_restore: Fresh sender replica is byte-identical to authoritative image and passes audit
Recovery leaves witness head and image unchanged
R1-R8 again match generated authoritative logical state
R9.relation_boundary: At an unavailable event the local replica may be stale: check R9, defer local R1-R8 until restore. Every other completed event checks R1-R8; RECOVER adds R9. Diagnostic full-image hashes are never generator inputs.

matrix.datasets: All 8 binary datasets for fixed N=3; approved result fixed to 1 (histogram [1,0,0,0]). Not a sampling-distribution experiment.
matrix.exception: exact_retry uses only before_witness_accept, after_witness_accept, after_local_anchor_write and response_drop; cached requests bypass new-dispatch effect/journal hooks.
matrix.expired_submit: Retry at 161 after a request creation window ending at 160. The action's own validity remains sufficient. If first commit exists, return original RECORDED; otherwise return unjournaled REJECTED without a mechanism invocation.

not_covered: Crashes during TICK/L1 private sampling, recipient acceptance, confirmation or recovery itself
Arbitrary request interleavings/concurrency, live identity changes, retirement and general induction
Public availability/error behavior for unplanned or private-data-dependent failures
Actual network closure/status/timing refinement or physical resource observations
Cross-host/power-loss faults, enforced process isolation from caller and nonrollback witness infrastructure
Full DP or cryptographic simulation proof and independent interoperability
